\title{Forward jets, missing $\pt$ and dijets from every vertex in high pileup:\\
\large a jet-vertex association by global missing-$\pt$ minimisation, tested against the truth}
\author{M.~Voutilainen \\ \small Helsinki Institute of Physics / CMS \\ \small \url{https://github.com/miquork/genseed}}
\date{\today}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent
PUPPI cannot tell vertices apart beyond the tracker: every particle-flow
candidate with $|\eta|>2.5$ gets the same weight at every vertex. On a
NeutrinoGun sample with $\langle N_{\mathrm{PU}}\rangle = 45$ and the generated
particles of every interaction, a per-vertex reconstruction therefore carries
the same forward jets at every vertex: \nul{50 times} the generated jets of the
vertex's own interaction at $2.5<|\eta|<3.0$ above 10\,GeV, made in 71\% of the
cases of several interactions at once, and a missing-$\pt$ of 15\,GeV rms per
component against 3\,GeV of true imbalance. We implemented the association of
the forward energy to vertices by a global minimisation of the summed
missing-$\pt$ $\chi^2$ over all vertices (JVA), with an exact, deterministic
optimiser, and tested it against the generator truth of every interaction.
\nul{It does not work at these momenta}: the forward energy that belongs to one
interaction carries 1.6\,GeV per vertex against 7\,GeV of recoil noise, every
recoil definition (particle missing-$\pt$, or the missing-$H_{\mathrm{T}}$ of
jets above 3--15\,GeV) correlates with it at $r = 0.13$--$0.16$, and the best
configuration places 1.4\% more single-interaction clusters right than wrong.
Two results do work. \hl{Extending PUPPI's charged-vertex association and its
$\alpha$ from $|\eta|<2.5$ to $|\eta|<3.0$}, using the charged candidates that
exist there, cuts the 2.5--3.0 spike by a factor 25--80 at every vertex
(reco/gen above 10\,GeV $49.6 \to 2.0$) and the missing-$\pt$ at the primary
vertex from 17.0 to 15.1\,GeV. And \hl{dijets selected at every vertex} give 130
times more low-$\pt$ balanced dijets per crossing than the primary vertex alone;
their bisector width reproduces the true jet resolution in the barrel from
$\pt^{\mathrm{avg}} = 5$\,GeV. The L3 residual needs Z+jet events, which this
sample does not have.
\end{abstract}

\section{The problem}

genseed reconstructs every usable vertex $v$ (34 per crossing, 31 of them owned
by an interaction) with PUPPI weights $w_i(v)$. Inside $|\eta|<2.5$ a charged
candidate belongs to a vertex and a neutral one is weighted by the charged
activity of that vertex around it. Beyond, PUPPI's weight $w^{\mathrm{fwd}}_i$
does not depend on $v$. Measured on the sample (300 crossings):

\begin{itemize}
\item every vertex carries 3.6 forward jets above 5\,GeV at $2.5<|\eta|<3.0$
  and 1.7 at $3<|\eta|<5$, 98--100\% of their $\pt$ from vertex-blind
  candidates; their cone holds 4.2 tracker tracks, 4.1 of them associated to
  other vertices;
\item from the genseed links, the dominant interaction of such a jet carries
  less than 40\% of its linked generated $\pt$ in 71\% of the jets and more than
  60\% in 7\%; three interactions contribute more than 10\% each. The spike is
  pileup made of several interactions, not misplaced jets;
\item the particle missing-$\pt$ per vertex has 25\,GeV rms per component at the
  primary vertex, against 3.2\,GeV of true imbalance of an interaction inside
  $|\eta|<5$;
\item the missing-$\pt$ of the vertex-resolved part ($|\eta|<2.5$) scatters
  around the owner's true central recoil by $\sigma \simeq \sqrt{1 + S_v}$\,GeV
  per component, $S_v$ the scalar sum of its weighted $\pt$ (5.8\,GeV at
  $S_v = 30$), while the true forward $\pt$ of an interaction is 4.8\,GeV rms.
\end{itemize}

\section{The jet-vertex association}

\paragraph{Objects.} The vertex-blind candidates ($|\eta| > \eta_{\mathrm{fwd}} =
2.5$, $w^{\mathrm{fwd}}>0$) are clustered once per crossing (anti-$k_{\mathrm T}$,
$R=0.4$, no threshold) into forward clusters $F_k$ with transverse momentum
$\vec p_k$: every such candidate is in exactly one cluster (24 per crossing).
For each vertex, $\vec M_v = -\sum w_i(v)\,\vec p_{\mathrm{T},i}$ over its
vertex-resolved candidates.

\paragraph{Objective.} An assignment $h_k \in \{\text{vertices}\} \cup \{\varnothing\}$
minimises
\begin{equation}
X(h) = \sum_v \frac{|\vec M_v - \sum_{k:\,h_k=v} \vec p_k|^2}{\sigma_v^2}
     + \sum_{k:\,h_k\ne\varnothing} \tau_k ,\qquad
\sigma_v^2 = \sigma_0^2 + \sigma_K^2 S_v ,
\end{equation}
so that a cluster is placed only where it improves the $\chi^2$ by more than its
price $\tau_k$, and a cluster that balances no vertex --- a combination of
interactions --- goes to nobody. Candidates: the vertices whose tracks lie in
the cluster (in the cone of the tracker tracks, \texttt{candMode 0}; its own
charged constituents with $2.5<|\eta|<3$, whose vertex reference PUPPI ignores,
\texttt{candMode 1}; either, \texttt{candMode 2}) at price $\tau_{\mathrm{trk}}$,
or any vertex at price $\tau_{\mathrm{all}}$ for a cluster without candidates.
Recoil: the particle missing-$\pt$ above (\texttt{recoilMode 0}) or the
missing-$H_{\mathrm{T}}$ of the vertex-resolved jets above $T$
(\texttt{recoilMode 1}, $\sigma_v^2 = \sigma_0^2 + \sigma_J^2\sum \pt^2 +
\sigma_K^2(S_v - H_{\mathrm{T}})$).

\paragraph{Optimiser} (\texttt{jvassoc.h}, ROOT-free). Clusters interact only
through shared vertices, so the problem splits exactly into connected
components (union-find over shared candidates); a component is solved
exhaustively over the product of its options up to $2\times10^5$ combinations,
otherwise by coordinate descent from the best single moves with pairwise
re-optimisation. On random instances the exhaustive path equals brute force in
every case and the descent reaches the optimum in 98.6\%; on the data, 30
perturbed restarts per crossing never found a lower objective. The result is
deterministic (ties to $\varnothing$, then to the lowest vertex).

\paragraph{Methods compared} (each gives an event for every vertex, which is
clustered and whose missing-$\pt$ is taken):
\texttt{dup} --- every vertex keeps all forward candidates (per-vertex PUPPI as
it is, and CMS PUPPI at the primary vertex); \texttt{lv} --- the forward
candidates go to the primary vertex only (the leading-vertex approach);
\texttt{trk} --- a cluster goes to the candidate with the most track evidence;
\texttt{jva}; \texttt{none} --- the forward energy goes to nobody; and two
oracles from the links, \texttt{ojet} (a cluster to the vertex of its dominant
interaction when that holds more than half of its linked $\pt$, else nobody)
and \texttt{opart} (every candidate to its own dominant interaction's vertex).
Knobs, histograms and tuple: \texttt{JVA.h}.

\section{Results}

All numbers: 25\,000 crossings (856\,527 vertices), \texttt{rootfiles/JVA\_v2.root};
the full tables and figures are in the appendix.

\subsection{Missing \texorpdfstring{$\pt$}{pT}}
Per component, rms over all vertices / at the primary vertex, in GeV:
\texttt{dup} 14.90 / 17.03, \texttt{lv} 7.18 / 17.03, \texttt{jva} 6.89 / 13.22,
\texttt{none} 6.96 / 13.55, \texttt{ojet} 6.92 / 12.96, \texttt{opart} 6.88 / 12.76
(Table~\ref{tab:jva_met}). \hl{Removing the forward duplicates halves the
missing-$\pt$ width over all vertices}, and at the primary vertex dropping the
forward energy (\texttt{none}) is as good as any association. The width is
\nul{not a figure of merit} for a method that minimises it: lowering the prices
pushes \texttt{jva} below the oracles by fitting noise, and even the residual
against the owner's true imbalance is circular, because the truth (3.2\,GeV)
is small against the noise (7\,GeV).

\subsection{The association against the truth}
With the default prices ($\tau_{\mathrm{trk}}=4$, $\tau_{\mathrm{all}}=12$)
\texttt{jva} places 0.2\% of the forward clusters above 5\,GeV right and drops
nearly everything; its correct fraction (right plus combinations dropped) is
0.741 against 0.762 for \texttt{none}. The offline re-optimisation from the
tuple, \texttt{scanJVA.C}, over the recoil (the particle missing $\pt$, or the
missing $H_{\mathrm{T}}$ of the jets above 3, 5, 7, 10 or 15\,GeV), the
candidates, the prices and the resolution scale, finds at best a net $+415\pm42$ of
29\,899 single-interaction clusters right (1.4\%; the missing $H_{\mathrm{T}}$ of jets above
15\,GeV, in-cluster charged candidates), while keeping 9.7\% of the combinations
and assigning single-interaction clusters and combinations at the same rate: the
balance does not know which vertex. The reason is quantitative:

\begin{center}\small
\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}
\toprule
recoil $R_v$ & $\vec M_v$ & $H_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}}$, $T=3$ & 5 & 7 & 10 & 15\,GeV \\
\midrule
correlation with the owner's true forward $\pt$ & \hl{0.457} & 0.396 & 0.345 & 0.298 & 0.239 & 0.176 \\
correlation with what the clusters can supply, $F_v$ & 0.138 & 0.133 & 0.133 & 0.136 & 0.144 & 0.159 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{center}

\noindent The missing-$H_{\mathrm{T}}$ of low-threshold jets is worse than the
particle missing-$\pt$ at every threshold: the recoil of forward minimum-bias
activity is soft (even the generated jets above 10\,GeV carry only $r=0.35$ of
it). And the forward $\pt$ that PUPPI leaves and that belongs to one interaction,
$F_v$, is only 1.6\,GeV per component per vertex (its forward floor,
$w\pt > 1.85 + 0.070\,N_{\mathrm{PV}} = 3.9$\,GeV, removes most of it): nothing
that measures a recoil of 7\,GeV noise can find it. Tracks alone do better: the
vertex holding most of a cluster's own charged $\pt$ is the right one for 31\%
of the single-interaction clusters above 5\,GeV (in-cone tracker tracks: 7\%),
and assigning by it (else nobody) gives a net $+5324\pm110$ (17.8\%), but keeps
77\% of the combinations.

\subsection{The forward spike, and PUPPI with tracks to \texorpdfstring{$|\eta|=3$}{|eta|=3}}
Reconstructed over generated jets per owned vertex at $2.5<|\eta|<3.0$ above
10\,GeV: \texttt{dup} 49.6, \texttt{lv} 1.53 (all of it at the primary vertex),
\texttt{jva} 0.10, \texttt{ojet} 0.24, \texttt{opart} 0.15, \texttt{none} 0: the
spike disappears only by dropping, and even the oracles recover a quarter of the
generated jets. The handle is the charged candidates at $2.5<|\eta|<3$: giving
PUPPI's vertex association and its $\alpha$ the same reach
(\texttt{pupEtaVtxAssoc = pupEtaTracker = etaFwd = 3}, \texttt{cmpPuppiFwd.C}):

\begin{center}\small
\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{\begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
\toprule
PUPPI & reco/gen $>$5 & $>$10 & $>$20\,GeV & own fraction & missing-$\pt$ rms, all / PV \\
\midrule
default (vertex-blind beyond 2.5), \texttt{dup} & 22.5 & 49.6 & 64.7 & 0.03 & 14.90 / 17.03 \\
tracks and $\alpha$ to $|\eta|<3$, \texttt{dup} & \hl{1.07} & \hl{1.99} & \hl{0.80} & 0.18 & 11.56 / \hl{15.06} \\
same, central neutral floor in 2.5--3 & 1.58 & 2.77 & 1.20 & 0.18 & 11.73 / 15.24 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{center}

\noindent The residual excess sits at $2.7<|\eta|<2.9$ (2.6 times the
generated jets above 5\,GeV), and the region beyond $|\eta|=3$, where no track
exists, keeps its own spike (4--8 times at $3.0<|\eta|<3.3$ with \texttt{dup}).
The forward neutral floor is to be kept: the central one lets more pileup in.
Whether CMS's PUPPI already associates the charged candidates beyond 2.5 depends
on its region configuration; in the genseed implementation it did not, and this
one change is the largest improvement found in this study.

\subsection{Dijets from every vertex}
Two leading jets above 3\,GeV (corrected), $\Delta\phi>2.7$, a tag at
$|\eta|<1.305$, $\alpha = \pt^{(3)}/\pt^{\mathrm{avg}} < 0.3$: 0.62 dijets per
crossing from all vertices (\texttt{lv}), against 0.0047 at the primary vertex
alone, where the forward junk takes the leading and the third jet (0.019 with
\texttt{jva} or \texttt{none}). \hl{Every pileup vertex is an independent
minimum-bias dijet event}: 130 times the primary vertex's yield at low $\pt$.
The L2Res closure, the mean $|R_{\mathrm{MPF}}/r_{\mathrm{true}} - 1|$ over the
probe bins at $\pt^{\mathrm{avg}} = 8$--10\,GeV, is 0.03 without an $\alpha$ cut
and 0.10 with $\alpha<0.3$ (statistics) for \texttt{lv}, \texttt{none} and
\texttt{ojet}; beyond $|\eta| = 2.5$ no probe bin reaches 50 dijets, because
PUPPI leaves no forward jets to probe. The JER from the bisector: with both jets
in the same $|\eta|$ bin (0.08 per crossing, 2100 in the sample), the
dijet-balance width $\sqrt{(\mathrm{RMS}_\parallel^2 -
\mathrm{RMS}_\perp^2)/2}$ matches the true resolution (rms/mean of
$\pt^{\mathrm{corr}}/\pt^{\mathrm{linkz}}$) within 10\% from
$\pt^{\mathrm{avg}} = 5$\,GeV in the barrel; the missing-$\pt$ version (MPFX)
comes out $\sim$25\% low and never within 10\%, presumably because the soft
activity in $\met$ is correlated with the dijet imbalance, not isotropic; the
core-fit versions need more than 200 dijets per bin and are empty. A statistically
useful low-$\pt$ JER and L2Res map needs about ten times this sample.

\section{Conclusions}
\begin{enumerate}
\item A jet-vertex association of the forward, vertex-blind energy by global
  missing-$\pt$ (or missing-$H_{\mathrm{T}}$) balance does not work for 5--20\,GeV
  forward jets at $\langle N_{\mathrm{PU}}\rangle = 45$: the balance cannot see the
  1.6\,GeV per vertex that belongs to single interactions. It may still help for
  hard forward jets in hard-scatter events, which this sample cannot test.
\item The forward spike at $2.5<|\eta|<3.0$ is mostly pileup made of several
  interactions. What removes it is information on the particles, not on the jets:
  PUPPI's vertex association extended to the charged candidates up to
  $|\eta|=3$ reduces it by a factor 25--80. This should be tried in CMSSW.
\item Dijets from every vertex are the way to low-$\pt$ JER and L2Res: two orders of
  magnitude more balanced dijets than the primary vertex, and a bisector JER that
  agrees with the truth from 5\,GeV. The missing-$\pt$ projections (MPF, MPFX) need
  care at these momenta. L3Res requires Z+jet events with pileup.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Code.} \texttt{jvassoc.h} (optimiser; \texttt{jva.h} cannot coexist
with \texttt{JVA.h} on a case-insensitive disk), \texttt{JVA.h/.C} (analyzer),
\texttt{runJVA.C}, \texttt{runjva.sh} (knobs; any knob via
\texttt{JVAOPT="key=value,..."}), \texttt{drawJVA.C} (this appendix),
\texttt{scanJVA.C} (offline re-optimisation from the tuple),
\texttt{cmpPuppiFwd.C} (the PUPPI comparison).
